source: ESA Collision Avoidance Challenge training archive
selectionPolicy: Champion selected only by validation F2, then validation PR-AUC and recall.

models.name: Logistic Regression
models.reason: Tests whether the engineered CDM state separates high-risk events without nonlinear complexity.

models.name: Random Forest
models.reason: Captures nonlinear feature interactions and remains stable under mixed scales and outliers.

models.name: Histogram Gradient Boosting
models.reason: Provides a strong native tree-boosting comparison without sharing LightGBM's implementation.

models.name: LightGBM
models.reason: Matches the existing explainable triage pipeline and handles sparse, nonlinear CDM features efficiently.

models.name: Multi-Layer Perceptron
models.reason: Tests a neural representation of the same leakage-safe T-2 feature set.

literature.title: Spacecraft Collision Avoidance Challenge: design and results
literature.finding: Defines the real CDM sequence prediction problem and documents the challenge results.

literature.title: ESA Collision Avoidance Challenge data
literature.finding: Provides 162,634 CDMs, 13,154 events, 103 fields and the operational T-2 cutoff.

literature.title: Implementation and comparison of data-based methods
literature.finding: Compares Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, MLP and LSTM approaches for conjunction data.

literature.title: Bayesian machine learning for satellite collision risk
literature.finding: Reports the strength of naive persistence and studies sequential probabilistic modelling.

limitations: The benchmark predicts final high-risk class from ESA CDM histories available at T-2.
Scores are not calibrated collision probabilities.
Public SOCRATES events do not contain the complete model feature set.
